newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya, Mauritania held reconciliation talks in Tunis.
newsitem.headline: Libya, Mauritania held reconciliation talks in Tunis.

text.p: Mauritanian and Libyan officials agreed to ease tension between their two countries at high-level talks in Tunis over the weekend, North African diplomats said on Tuesday.

The reconcilation came a a result of a mediation by Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali during a visit at the start of March by Mauritanian President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya, diplomats said.

The sources said Ibrahim Bishari, head of the office of Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, and Sidi Ould Khalifa, Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, met on Sunday in the presence of Tunisian Foreign Affairs Minister Abderrahim Zouari.
"The mediation was successful. Libyans and Mauritanians have agreed to open a new page in their relations," a diplomat close to the talks told Reuters.

Libya in November 1995 recalled its ambassador from Nouakchott and said it would cut off economic aid to the North African state in retaliation for Mauritania's decision to establish ties with Israel.
Nouakchott accuses Tripoli of trying to destabilise it and last month cracked down on Mauritanian opponents allegedly accused of ties with Libya.

The two countries, along with Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco, are members of the Arab Maghreb Union (AMU) established in 1989 but which has its activities almost freezed during the last three years because of bilateral disputes, and especially between Algeria and Morocco over the Sahara issue.
"The reconciliation between Libya and Mauritania contributes to a better atmosphere in the AMU," a North African diplomat said.
